title: Resolving vectors into perpendicular components enrichment

evidence.role: Direct retrieval is grounded in the independently verified Lesson 10 handoff rather than a new P2 assignment.

hints: The second vector must begin where the first vector ends.
The resultant connects the overall start to the overall finish.

walkthrough.text: Draw A first and preserve its magnitude and direction.
Translate B parallel to itself until the tail of B meets the head of A, without rotating, stretching or reversing B.
Draw the resultant from the tail of A to the final head of B and point its arrow towards that final head.

ai_rubric.observable: Places the tail of B at the head of A while preserving the magnitude and direction of B
Draws the resultant from the tail of A to the final head of B with the correct arrow direction

evidence.role: Grounds selection of the component adjacent to an angle measured from the horizontal, using original values and context.

hints: Treat the 10 N vector as the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle.
The horizontal side is adjacent to the stated angle.

walkthrough.text: The 30 degree angle is measured from the horizontal, so the horizontal component is adjacent to it.
Use the adjacent-to-hypotenuse ratio: horizontal component = $10\cos30^\circ$.
$10\cos30^\circ=8.660...\,\mathrm{N}$, so option A is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects A, identifying the horizontal component as $10\cos30^\circ=8.66\,\mathrm{N}$

evidence.role: Grounds two perpendicular components when the stated angle is measured from north rather than east.

hints: Mark the 40 degree angle beside the north axis.
Identify which component is adjacent and which is opposite before selecting an expression.

walkthrough.text: The angle is measured east of north, so the north component lies adjacent to the angle and the east component lies opposite.
The adjacent north component is $20\cos40^\circ$ and the opposite east component is $20\sin40^\circ$.
Option B lists those expressions with the correct directions.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects B, using $20\sin40^\circ$ east and $20\cos40^\circ$ north for an angle measured from north

evidence.role: Grounds components as axis-dependent projections whose signed sums represent the original vector.

hints: Ask what happens when the two component arrows are added head-to-tail.
Changing the axes changes the projections but not the original vector.

walkthrough.text: A component is a projection along a chosen axis, so rotating the axes can change the two component values.
The two perpendicular component arrows form the sides of a right-angled vector triangle.
Their vector sum is the hypotenuse, which is the unchanged original vector, so option A is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects A, stating that perpendicular components depend on the chosen axes and add vectorially to the original vector

evidence.role: Grounds a complete two-component construction and calculation for an angle measured from the horizontal.

hints: Complete a right-angled triangle from the head of the given vector to the axes.
Decide which component is adjacent to the 28 degree angle.

walkthrough.text: Draw rightward and upward component arrows so their head-to-tail sum ends at the head of the 46 N vector.
Use cosine for the adjacent horizontal component and sine for the opposite vertical component.
Keep N on both results and check that the two perpendicular components reconstruct a 46 N vector at 28 degrees.

evidence.role: Grounds a perpendicular component triangle while the original diagram and context remain new.

hints: Both component arrows must lie along the supplied axes.
Their head-to-tail route must end at the head of the given vector.

walkthrough.text: From the origin, draw a horizontal arrow to the right.
From its head, draw a vertical arrow upwards until it reaches the head of the 46 N vector.
Label the arrows as horizontal and vertical components and confirm they are perpendicular.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws a rightward horizontal component and an upward vertical component as perpendicular sides
Labels the component arrows so their head-to-tail sum reconstructs the stated 46 N vector

evidence.role: Grounds calculation of a component beside an angle measured from the horizontal.

hints: The horizontal component is next to the 28 degree angle.
Use the trigonometric ratio involving the adjacent side and hypotenuse.

walkthrough.text: The horizontal component is adjacent to 28 degrees and the 46 N vector is the hypotenuse.
Calculate $F_x=46\cos28^\circ=40.615589...\,\mathrm{N}$.
Report 40.6 N to the right, or 41 N to two significant figures.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses $F_x=46\cos28^\circ$ for the component adjacent to the stated angle
Obtains a horizontal component of 40.6 N to the right

evidence.role: Grounds calculation of a component opposite an angle measured from the horizontal.

hints: The vertical component lies opposite the 28 degree angle.
Use the ratio involving the opposite side and hypotenuse.

walkthrough.text: The vertical component is opposite 28 degrees and the 46 N vector is the hypotenuse.
Calculate $F_y=46\sin28^\circ=21.595692...\,\mathrm{N}$.
Report 21.6 N upwards, or 22 N to two significant figures.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses $F_y=46\sin28^\circ$ for the component opposite the stated angle
Obtains a vertical component of 21.6 N upwards

evidence.role: Grounds reverse quadrant direction, angle reference and a two-component trigonometric calculation.

hints: Read the angle from west, not from south.
Use the diagram to attach westward and southward directions after calculating magnitudes.

walkthrough.text: Draw the westward and southward sides of the component triangle in the southwest quadrant.
The west component is adjacent to 58 degrees, while the south component is opposite.
Calculate with cosine and sine, retain m and state both compass directions or use an explicit signed east-north convention.

evidence.role: Grounds a perpendicular two-axis representation with the original quadrant and values changed.

hints: Both component arrows must point into the same west and south directions as the vector's projections.
Make their endpoint match the head of the 72 m vector.

walkthrough.text: Draw one component west from the origin.
From its head, draw the second component south to the head of the 72 m vector.
Label the two perpendicular arrows westward and southward.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws westward and southward component arrows as perpendicular sides
Labels the components so their vector sum reconstructs the stated southwest vector

evidence.role: Grounds selection of the adjacent component from a stated axis angle.

hints: The 58 degree angle begins at the west axis.
The westward side is adjacent to that angle.

walkthrough.text: Identify the westward component as adjacent to the 58 degree angle.
Calculate $s_W=72\cos58^\circ=38.154187...\,\mathrm{m}$.
Report 38.2 m west, or minus 38.2 m on an east-positive axis.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses $s_W=72\cos58^\circ$ because the westward component is adjacent to the stated angle
Obtains a westward component magnitude of 38.2 m

evidence.role: Grounds selection of the opposite component and preservation of direction.

hints: The southward component is across from the 58 degree angle.
Its magnitude is positive, but its signed north-axis value would be negative.

walkthrough.text: Identify the southward component as opposite the 58 degree angle.
Calculate $s_S=72\sin58^\circ=61.059463...\,\mathrm{m}$.
Report 61.1 m south, or minus 61.1 m on a north-positive axis.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses $s_S=72\sin58^\circ$ because the southward component is opposite the stated angle
Obtains a southward component magnitude of 61.1 m

evidence.role: Grounds resolving a vector, combining signed components and reconstructing a resultant, while Lesson 10 supplies the prior vector-addition dependency.

hints: Resolve A before adding the westward vector.
Treat west as negative if east is chosen positive, and retain the unchanged north component.

walkthrough.text: Resolve A into east and north components using the 40 degree angle from east.
Add the 12 m west vector to the east-west component with signs, while leaving the north component unchanged.
Use the final perpendicular components to calculate the resultant magnitude and its angle north of east.

evidence.role: Grounds resolution into two compass-axis components for an angle measured from east.

hints: The east component is adjacent to 40 degrees.
The north component is opposite the angle.

walkthrough.text: Use $A_E=30\cos40^\circ=22.981333...\,\mathrm{m}$ east.
Use $A_N=30\sin40^\circ=19.283628...\,\mathrm{m}$ north.
Retain extra digits for the later addition and report both directions.

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains the eastward component of A as $30\cos40^\circ=22.98\,\mathrm{m}$
Obtains the northward component of A as $30\sin40^\circ=19.28\,\mathrm{m}$

evidence.role: Grounds signed component combination, with direct Lesson 10 addition supplying the declared prior dependency.

hints: East and west are opposite directions on one axis.
Vector B has no northward component.

walkthrough.text: Choose east as positive, so vector B contributes minus 12 m on the east-west axis.
Calculate the final east component as $22.981333-12=10.981333\,\mathrm{m}$ east.
Because B is purely westward, retain $19.283628\,\mathrm{m}$ north as the final north component.

ai_rubric.observable: Combines the opposing east-west components as $22.9813-12$ to obtain 10.9813 m east
Retains the final northward component as 19.2836 m north

evidence.role: Grounds reconstruction of a resultant magnitude from perpendicular combined components.

hints: The final east and north components are perpendicular sides.
The resultant magnitude is the hypotenuse.

walkthrough.text: Use the final components 10.981333 m east and 19.283628 m north.
Report 22.2 m to three significant figures and confirm it is longer than either component.

ai_rubric.observable: Forms $R=\sqrt{10.9813^2+19.2836^2}$ from the final perpendicular components
Obtains a resultant magnitude of 22.2 m

evidence.role: Grounds reconstruction of direction from perpendicular components with a clearly stated angle reference.

hints: For an angle measured from east, the north component is opposite and east is adjacent.
Finish with the compass phrase, not only a degree value.

walkthrough.text: Let theta be measured from the positive east direction towards north.
Report $60.3^\circ$ north of east, which matches the positive north and east components.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses $\tan\theta=19.2836/10.9813$ for an angle measured north of east
Obtains a direction of $60.3^\circ$ north of east

later_learning_excluded: later-topic force, motion, momentum, field and energy laws
physical applications not supplied entirely within the question

quality_audit.originality: All learner prompts, values and planned diagram briefs are original. No official Cambridge wording, numerical set or figure is reproduced.
quality_audit.scope: The package teaches only representation of a coplanar vector as two perpendicular components, with reconstruction and prior vector addition used as checks and one declared mixed dependency.
quality_audit.evidence: All eight mapped P2 leaves, their enrichment records, complete canonical question contexts and relevant official marking demands were reviewed. Later-topic physics in mixed questions was isolated and excluded. P1 remains deferred and no P1 lesson assignment was inferred.
quality_audit.numerical_recomputation: All generated results were independently recomputed. Notes: 52 cos 32 = 44.0985010, 52 sin 32 = 27.5558017, 64 cos 25 = 58.0036984, 64 sin 25 = 27.0475688, 70 cos 40 = 53.6231110 and 70 sin 40 = 44.9951327. Adding 18 m east gives signed components -35.6231110 m and -44.9951327 m, with resultant 57.3896158 m at 51.6309770 degrees south of west. Practice: 10 cos 30 = 8.6602540; 46 cos 28 = 40.6155893 and 46 sin 28 = 21.5956919, reconstructing 46 N at 28 degrees; 72 cos 58 = 38.1541870 and 72 sin 58 = 61.0594629, reconstructing 72 m at 58 degrees; q07 gives 22.9813333 m east and 19.2836283 m north for A, then 10.9813333 m east and 19.2836283 m north, resultant 22.1911694 m at 60.3400420 degrees north of east.
quality_audit.dependency_audit: Exactly two learner-visible questions exercise dependency: q01 directly retrieves Lesson 10 head-to-tail addition, while q07 combines current component resolution with Lesson 10 signed vector addition and resultant reconstruction.
later_knowledge_excluded: equilibrium, moments, momentum conservation, weight and motion laws from mixed P2 contexts
any later-topic physical principle not fully supplied
